Topic map

  • Physics & windows: piezoelectric transducer, time-of-flight, acoustic windows, image limitations.
  • Standard views: parasternal long/short, apical 4/2/5, subcostal, suprasternal.
  • M-mode: one line through time, valve motion, LV dimensions, EF demonstration.
  • Doppler: PW vs CW, spectral timing, BART color convention, regurgitation.
  • Recognition: LV dilation/LVH, RV dilation, bicuspid aortic valve, pericardial effusion/tamponade, wall-motion abnormalities, aortic dissection limits.

Acoustic-window logic

HelpfulWhy
GelRemoves air interface between probe and skin.
Soft tissue / liverAllows sound transmission; liver helps the subcostal window.
HarderWhy
Ribs / boneStrong reflection blocks the beam.
Air / COPDAir disrupts transmission; hyperinflation worsens windows.
Extreme depthLecture emphasizes finite penetration, especially in very large patients.

8. Exam sheet

One-page mental model

Windows

  • Parasternal: 4th–5th ICS near sternum. PLAX → rotate 90° → PSAX.
  • Apical: PMI. 4C; tilt for “5C”; rotate for 2C.
  • Subcostal: under ribs through liver; rescue view, IAS/IVC/effusion.
  • Suprasternal: aortic arch; RPA beneath; uncomfortable but useful.

PLAX anatomy

Near field = RV. Then septum/LV, MV, LA, AV/LVOT/aortic root. Walls emphasized: septal + posterior/inferior.

PSAX levels

Mid-LV = papillary muscles. Tilt toward base → mitral valve → aortic valve. Normal AV has 3 cusps; bicuspid has 2.

M-mode

One line through time. QRS anchors ventricular systole. Aortic valve opens in systole. Mitral leaflet: E = early filling; A = atrial kick.

EF = (EDV−ESV)/EDV. Example 100→40 = 60%.

Doppler

BART = Blue Away, Red Toward the transducer. PW samples a specific location; CW measures velocities along a line.

MR: systolic LV→LA flow. Do not memorize the jet as a fixed color; derive color from probe direction.

Pathology snapshots

  • LVH = thick wall; lecture rough normal ~1 cm.
  • Regional akinesis = ischemic injury / MI clue.
  • Tamponade = effusion + RA/RV collapse + respiratory variation.
  • Dissection: suprasternal TTE may hint, but TEE/CT is stronger.
Common traps: “screen side” is not anatomy; color is not pathology; one normal view does not rule out a regional wall-motion abnormality; a fluid collection does not automatically equal tamponade physiology; small EF differences can reflect measurement variability.
Lecture vs current guideline: the lecture uses Teichholz-style M-mode linear dimensions to demonstrate EF. This is useful for understanding the math and likely lecture testing, but ASE chamber-quantification guidance states that Teichholz/Quinones linear-dimension volume calculations are no longer recommended for clinical LV volume/EF assessment because fixed-geometry assumptions can fail.
9. Sources & clarifications

What was used, what was adapted, what needs a caveat

This section is intentionally separate from active practice.

Lecture materials used

  • 9-11-2026_Rubinstein_Echocardiography.pptx — full 79-slide deck reviewed; teaching content concentrated before the meme/closing slides.
  • Echocardiography-transcript.txt — used for professor emphasis, live-demo reasoning, timing, and image-quality comments.
  • 9-11-2026_Rubinstein_Echocardiography_objectives.docx — used to set required coverage.
  • Echocardiography_-_Practice_Questions.V1.docx — all five professor questions integrated; non-MCQ items were adapted to single-best-answer format.

Meaningful adaptations

The lecture is primarily about views and imaging modes, so the “condition/drug guide” was adapted into a combined view + pathology target guide. Original practice stems that asked free response were converted to MCQ without changing the keyed structure or answer.

Clarifications / discrepancies

Doppler direction wording

One slide says a blood cell moving “towards the heart” produces a higher frequency. The precise reference is movement toward the transducer, not toward the heart. The lecture’s later BART rule is correct.

ASE Doppler quantification guidance · ASE comprehensive TTE guidance

Teichholz EF demonstration

The lecture uses M-mode linear dimensions and the Teichholz conversion to teach how diameter can be converted to volume and then EF. ASE chamber-quantification guidance says Teichholz and Quinones methods are no longer recommended for clinical LV volumes because they assume a fixed LV geometry that can be inaccurate in pathology.

ASE/EACVI chamber quantification guideline

Short-axis textbook mismatch flagged by the professor

The transcript explicitly notes that one textbook pairing shows a papillary-muscle-level schematic next to a mitral-level echo image. The guide preserves the professor’s correction: probe tilt changes the short-axis level.

Figure verification limitation

Static slide images were used because the uploaded deck does not provide cine loops in this environment. Timing questions therefore use the ECG trace, valve position, and lecture narration rather than frame-by-frame video playback.
